observations: Initial full twenty-dollar basket held three four-dollar loaves and four two-dollar apples.
Raising loaves to four automatically reduced apples to two while spending stayed twenty.
Removing an apple left two dollars unused; changing to zero loaves and filling produced ten apples.
Screenshot encodes each item by its dollar width; reveal recalls the original full basket rather than confusing it with current contents, and explains the price ratio.
whyCool: A purchase can fit the budget and still cost you something already in the basket.
caveat: Made-up prices and two goods; no preference or real-price claim.
effort: Prediction, original displacement, spare-budget state, opposite endpoint, screenshot and reveal.
bucketReason: Concrete conditional opportunity cost with reversible allocation and clear visual accounting.

prediction.reason: Precise opportunity-cost question with clear initial full-budget condition.
prediction.evidence: None, one or two apples leave.

interaction.reason: Full allocation, spare money and opposite endpoint test the condition rather than only the original answer.
interaction.evidence: Four loaves/two apples, four/one with two dollars left, then zero/ten.

payoff.reason: Uses the original event and states the binding-budget condition and exchange ratio.
payoff.evidence: Once all money spent, four over two means two apples.

clarity.reason: Money-width diagram and spent/left counters track allocation.
clarity.evidence: Ten equal two-dollar slots at endpoint.

transfer.reason: Explicit general rule with its applicability condition.
transfer.evidence: Price ratio determines tradeoff when the fixed budget is fully used.

playfulness.reason: Build and rebalance a constrained basket.

practicalValue.evidence: Opportunity cost when money already allocated.
